subproblem.title: The closed unit cubes containing a point cover a neighbourhood of it (parent steps 5 and 6)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and x ∈ ℝ^P (Euclid P). There is a finite set Z ⊆ ℤ^P such that x ∈ z + [0,1]^P (i.e. z_i ≤ x_i ≤ z_i + 1 for all i) for every z ∈ Z, and every y in some neighbourhood of x lies in z + [0,1]^P for some z ∈ Z.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (x : Euclid P), ∃ Z : Finset (Fin P → ℤ), (∀ z ∈ Z, ∀ i, (z i : ℝ) ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ z i + 1) ∧ ∀ᶠ y : Euclid P in 𝓝 x, ∃ z ∈ Z, ∀ i, (z i : ℝ) ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ z i + 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the supplied proof of the selected parent dimred_mbl_dt_skeleton_retraction [its parent's Lemma D = Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 5.4, with the documented 3/4 → 1/4 erratum]: 'The closed unit cubes not containing x form a closed set missing x, so points y near x lie in the finitely many closed cubes containing x' (used for D̄ψ(x) ≤ max over those cubes, and again through step 5 in step 6). This child proves that local finiteness fact by an explicit coordinatewise construction.
1. One-dimensional claim. For t ∈ ℝ let A(t) := {k ∈ {⌊t⌋ − 1, ⌊t⌋} : k ≤ t ≤ k + 1} and V(t) := ⋃_{k ∈ A(t)} [k, k + 1]. Then V(t) is a neighbourhood of t. If t ∉ ℤ, then ⌊t⌋ < t < ⌊t⌋ + 1, so ⌊t⌋ ∈ A(t) and V(t) ⊇ (⌊t⌋, ⌊t⌋ + 1) ∋ t. If t ∈ ℤ, then ⌊t⌋ = t, both t − 1 and t lie in A(t), and V(t) ⊇ [t − 1, t + 1] ⊇ (t − 1, t + 1) ∋ t. (Int.floor_le, Int.lt_floor_add_one.)
2. Let Z be the set of z ∈ ℤ^P with z_i ∈ {⌊x_i⌋ − 1, ⌊x_i⌋} and z_i ≤ x_i ≤ z_i + 1 for all i. It is a subset of the finite product ∏_i {⌊x_i⌋ − 1, ⌊x_i⌋} (Fintype.piFinset, then Finset.filter), hence a Finset, and by construction x ∈ z + [0,1]^P for every z ∈ Z. This is the first conclusion. (For P = 0, Z is the singleton of the unique element of ℤ^0 and every condition below is vacuous.)
3. For each coordinate i the map y ↦ y_i is continuous, so by 1 the set W_i := {y : y_i ∈ V(x_i)} is a neighbourhood of x. Since there are finitely many coordinates, eventually in 𝓝 x the point y lies in W_i for all i simultaneously (Filter.eventually_all).
4. Let y ∈ W_i for all i. For each i choose k_i ∈ A(x_i) with k_i ≤ y_i ≤ k_i + 1 (possible because y_i ∈ V(x_i)) and put z := (k_i)_i. Then z_i ∈ {⌊x_i⌋ − 1, ⌊x_i⌋} and z_i ≤ x_i ≤ z_i + 1 for every i, so z ∈ Z, and z_i ≤ y_i ≤ z_i + 1 for every i. This is the second conclusion. ∎
